title: Frida Kahlo: Painter, Icon, Genius
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant profile Frida Kahlo, the Mexican painter known for raw self-portraits. They cover her childhood in Coyoacán and the Casa Azul, her father Guillermo (Carl Wilhelm) Kahlo, her 1925 bus-trolley accident and its effect on her career, her polio, her communist politics, her marriage to and divorce from muralist Diego Rivera, the Rockefeller Center mural controversy, the commission for "The Suicide of Dorothy Hale," her miscarriages and themes of pain and motherhood, her pets and famous paintings such as "The Two Fridas," "What the Water Gave Me," "My Birth," and "The Wounded Deer," her eyebrow, her late-life exhibition, her death at 47, and her posthumous rediscovery. The episode also includes listener mail and a plug for the podcast "Worth It."

segments.title: Opening banter and tour dates
segments.summary: The hosts mention upcoming live shows in Salt Lake City, Phoenix and Melbourne, then introduce the episode on Frida Kahlo and their family's fondness for her work, and discuss how pronunciation of her name and her appeal to artists and women shape the conversation.

segments.title: Early life, family and education
segments.summary: Kahlo's birth in Coyoacán and her claimed birth year, her German-born father Guillermo Kahlo who changed his name in Mexico and married Matilda Calderón, her strict mother, her father's influence and her schooling at the German College and the National Preparatory School, where she was sexually abused and became one of few girls admitted. Her interest in Mexican roots and her childhood polio are introduced.

segments.title: Revolutionary politics and Diego Rivera at school
segments.summary: Kahlo joins a student revolutionary group, the Cachuchas, and becomes a lifelong communist. At fifteen she watches Diego Rivera paint the mural Creation at her school and grows infatuated with him.

segments.title: Bus-trolley accident at eighteen
segments.summary: At eighteen Kahlo is impaled by a handrail when a bus and trolley collide. Her spine and pelvis are injured, and she gives up her plan to become a doctor. The hosts call it the most significant event of her life.

segments.title: Painting during recovery and meeting Rivera again
segments.summary: Bedridden for months, Kahlo begins painting self-portraits using a special easel and a ceiling mirror. She reconnects with Rivera at a party, shows him her work, and he encourages her, and they marry. The hosts discuss how her emotional, raw self-portraits broke with expectations for women artists.
topics: Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera marriage

segments.title: Marriage, affairs and life in the United States
segments.summary: The hosts describe the couple's mutual affairs, Rivera's praise of Kahlo as a realist artist, their moves to San Francisco, Detroit and New York for his murals, and her homesickness for Mexico. They mention her early notoriety and her acquaintance with Picasso.

segments.title: Rockefeller mural controversy and the film Frida
segments.summary: Nelson Rockefeller commissions Rivera's Man at the Crossroads at Rockefeller Center. Rivera includes Lenin, Rockefeller objects, and the mural is destroyed; Rivera later recreates it in Mexico City as Man, Controller of the Universe. The hosts discuss the 2002 film Frida, directed by Julie Taymor and starring Salma Hayek, with Edward Norton's role, and the film's production difficulties.

segments.title: The Suicide of Dorothy Hale and miscarriages
segments.summary: Clare Boothe Luce commissions Kahlo to paint a memorial to her friend Dorothy Hale, who died by suicide. Kahlo instead painted a graphic depiction of the death, which Luce nearly destroyed. The hosts then turn to Kahlo's miscarriages, including the one she painted in Henry Ford Hospital, and her desire to be a mother, with her many pets.

segments.title: Pain imagery and key paintings
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the physical and emotional pain in Kahlo's work, including nails, a crumbling Doric column spine, and exposed organs. They describe The Two Fridas, What the Water Gave Me, My Birth and The Wounded Deer. They also cover her Indigenous Mexican influences and her mix of styles, including surrealism and magic realism, and André Breton's labeling of her as a surrealist.

segments.title: Trotsky, the marriage, later life and death
segments.summary: The hosts cover Kahlo's friendship with Leon Trotsky, her divorce from Rivera in 1939 and remarriage in 1940, the affair with her sister that hurt her, and her declining health. Her 1953 exhibition, held with her bedridden, is noted. She died at 47, with the cause listed as pulmonary embolism and suspicion of suicide by pills, and her work was rediscovered in the late 1970s.

segments.title: Eyebrow, legacy and museums
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Kahlo's unibrow, citing Desmond Morris's remarks on women and fashion, and her legacy among female artists. They recommend seeing her work in museums and mention an article on the site.

segments.title: Listener mail: Mistakes in defense of us and Worth It podcast
segments.summary: A listener praises the show's research and recommends the Trail of Tears episodes. The hosts also plug Shelina's new podcast Worth It, about creating a happy life.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact information
segments.summary: The hosts give social media and email contact details and sign off.
